 Daily Stock Market Live
 Updated Wed, Oct 21 2026 5:44 PM EDT Share Share Article via Facebook Share Article via Twitter Share Article via LinkedIn Share Article via Email S&P 500 notches 3-day win streak, Nasdaq jumps 1% as SpaceX and Tesla rally
 Sean Conlon Hugh Leask Lee Ying Shan Deena Zaidi Traders work on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange, Aug. 7, 2026. Jeenah Moon | Reuters Stocks rose on Wednesday as the latest developments surrounding SpaceX and Tesla led investors to move back into technology. 
 The Nasdaq Composite added 1.05% to end at 26,702.86, and the S&P 500 rose 0.58% to 7,757.17. The Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed 360.21 points, or 0.69%, to close at 52,856.09.
 Shares of Elon Musk's SpaceX surged 7% after the company said its revenue grew 161% in the third quarter. Musk also said that SpaceX and Tesla, his auto manufacturer, have formed special committees to discuss a merger. Tesla, which is due to report earnings later, saw shares rise more than 3%.
 SpaceX's artificial intelligence business grew ninefold, reigniting enthusiasm for stocks related to the trade. Shares of Advanced Micro Devices advanced more than 3%, while Nvidia 's stock rose more than 2%. Shares of Micron Technology and Marvell Technology grew nearly 2%. The VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) was up close to 2% as well.
 "SpaceX suggests there is still a longer runway here, but that fundamental tension or experience of getting overly enthusiastic and overly capitalizing things I don't think has changed," said Joe Zidle, Cresset's chief market strategist.
 Concerns around the AI trade's sustainability have weighed on market sentiment lately, as traders focused on debt-backed AI investments and whether the infrastructure demand justifies companies' spending. But Zidle anticipates that the current reporting period will show that a number of AI-related companies are continuing to see stronger demand.
 "I think when we get to the end of earnings season and we look back, SpaceX is not an anomaly; it's not a phenomenon; it's actually something that's going to be, I think, more common to the sector," he said.
 Investors are seeking more insights into the AI trade on Wednesday, with Meta Platforms also set to report after the bell. Earlier this month, the company rolled out its latest AI model , Muse Wonder, which is only available to paying users.
 Traders are also watching for results from IBM and Southwest Airlines , both of which are due after the close.
 Netflix was a key laggard during Wednesday's session. Shares tumbled more than 5% after the streaming mainstay's full-year revenue forecast came in below analysts' expectations. The company also cut its ad revenue guidance for the full year.
 8 Hours Ago Stocks finish higher
 The three leading U.S. indexes rose on Wednesday.
 The S&P 500 added 0.58% to finish at 7,757.17, while the Nasdaq Composite jumped 1.05% to 26,702.86. The Dow Jones Industrial Average increased 360.21 points, or 0.69%, to 52,856.09.
 — Sean Conlon 
 9 Hours Ago CME Group's Terry Duffy warns of risks of leverage and financial product innovation
 Terry Duffy, CEO of CME Group Inc., speaks during the Piper Sandler Global Exchange and FinTech Conference in New York City, U.S., June 5, 2025. Adam Gray | Reuters CME Group 's outgoing CEO Terry Duffy said innovation needs to be balanced with effective regulation to protect market integrity and participants, speaking to CNBC's "Power Lunch" Wednesday. 
 His comments come amid a wave of innovation in financial products like perpetual futures contracts and tokenized assets – ideas made popular in the crypto market that have challenged the status quo in the traditional market, particularly demand for always-on markets. Duffy said the push to compete in the 24/7 trading boom mustn't outpace regulation, however, especially as retail access increases.
 "Innovation is critically important, it's the lifeblood to any institution … You've got to be careful not to have innovation for the sake of innovation without regulation. And sometimes that's what I'm seeing with the products," he said.
 He raised concerns about the CFTC's handling of more than 4,000 self-certified contracts and the risks of extreme leverage without enforceable limits to protect retail traders and broader financial stability.
 "Innovation is great," Duffy added, "as long as it's not at the cost of efficiencies and credibility to the marketplace."
 — Tanaya Macheel 
 9 Hours Ago Nvidia, SpaceX are two biggest Nasdaq contributors Wednesday
 The Nasdaq Composite was up more than 1% in afternoon trading on Wednesday, and two names in particular were contributing the most to that move.
 Nvidia supported the tech-heavy index's gains the most, rising more than 2%. SpaceX was the second-largest contributor with its more than 7% jump.
 The moves come after SpaceX reported a massive jump in revenue as well as its artificial intelligence business for the third quarter, leading investors to move into SpaceX as well as other AI-related stocks.
 — Sean Conlon 
 10 Hours Ago Stocks making big moves: Roivant Sciences, Bloom Energy, Strategy
 Thomas Fuller | SOPA Images | Lightrocket | Getty Images Here are some of the companies making headlines in midday trading: 
 Roivant Sciences — Shares rose more than 4% after the company's immune-modifying pill Lisraya reached its primary efficacy goals in two Phase 3 trials for non-infectious uveitis, a disease of the eye.
 Bloom Energy — The fuel cell company jumped more than 6% as traders snapped up shares ahead of Thursday's third-quarter report. The FactSet consensus sees earnings coming in at 69 cents per share on revenue of $1.07 billion. Wolfe Research dubbed the company a "recent outperformer" in its preview of clean energy earnings, saying "demand signal continues to build, beat and raise potential."
 Bitcoin-linked stocks — Bitcoin jumped more than 2% to trade above $84,000 as investors flocked to risk assets. A raft of crypto-related stocks leapt alongside it, with Strategy gaining 7% and bitcoin miner MARA Holdings rising more than 3%. Riot Platforms advanced 2%.
 Read the full list here .
 — Davis Giangiulio 
 11 Hours Ago Barclays sees catalysts ahead for tech bonds
 Fears about massive artificial intelligence spending has sent spreads wider in the credit market, but Barclays is expecting a shift in sentiment in the coming weeks. 
 That could lead to some tactical, short-term opportunities in tech credit, analyst Andrew Keches said in a note Tuesday. 
 "The demand side of the AI equation remains incredibly strong, IG [investment grade] balance sheets remain entrenched, and there are near-term catalysts that could restore market confidence," he wrote. 
 Those include hyperscaler earnings, such as Meta 's results coming after the bell, and Oracle investor day, expected Oct. 28. Alphabet and Microsoft also report quarterly earnings on Oct. 28.
 Apple is set to report on Nov. 2, while Oracle hasn't set a release date yet for its next quarterly results. 
 That said, Keches doubts this is the last round of volatility and he remains underweight tech in the medium term. "[F]unding will remain an overhang through 2027."
 — Michelle Fox 
 12 Hours Ago Berkshire Hathaway shares hit new all-time high Wednesday
 Greg Abel, CEO of Berkshire Hathaway, speaks with CNBC from the Berkshire Hathaway Annual Shareholders Meeting in Omaha Nebraska on May 1, 2026. David A. Grogan | CNBC Berkshire Hathaway Class A and B shares both made 52-week highs Wednesday. 
 Class B stock advanced 0.5% to $543 per share while Class A stock ticked 0.6% higher to $814,594 apiece. 
 The conglomerate's shares have been bucking the broader market's volatility, logging 10 consecutive days of gains, ending last week.
 Berkshire Hathaway shares closed Friday at their highest level since Warren Buffett said at the firm's annual meeting in May 2025 that he planned to step down as CEO by the end of the year.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon BRK.A, 1-year — Paulina Likos 
 12 Hours Ago Oppenheimer upgrades Zoom in bet on its AI transformation
 Oppenheimer says that Zoom Communications' AI platform is "working better than expected," and it's changing the outlook for the stock. 
 The bank upgraded the stock to outperform from perform, and placed a $130 price target on the stock. That implies a 33% gain from Tuesday's close. Analyst Timothy Horan wrote in a Wednesday note that Oppenheimer is gaining confidence in Zoom's transition from a video meeting platform to a larger AI communications and workflow one. 
 "Its AI platform is enjoying strong uptake, growing ARPU," average revenue per user, "and retention," Horan said in the note. "Integrating communications with AI applications should deepen customer relationships and raise the growth rate to double digits, all on stable margins."
 Horan also raised his long-term revenue estimates. Shares of Zoom were higher by more than 2% on Wednesday. 
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon Zoom Communications year-to-date. — Davis Giangiulio  
 13 Hours Ago United Airlines slashes profit outlook as fuel costs surge
 A United Airlines plane approaches the runway at Denver International Airport on March 23, 2026. Al Drago | Getty Images Shares of United Airlines up more than 4% on Wednesday.
 The carrier provided a weaker-than-expected fourth-quarter profit outlook as rising fuel costs weighed on profitability but reported revenue of a record $17.9 billion, which is a 17% increase year over year.
 "Our employees met the challenge of our ever-changing environment and our results prove the resilience of focusing on building a brand-loyal airline for customers," United CEO Scott Kirby said in an earnings release .
 United expects adjusted earnings of 50 cents to $1.50 per share in the fourth quarter, below the $1.76 analysts expected.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon UAL stock price The airline reported third-quarter adjusted earnings of $2.54 per share, missing estimates of $2.57.
 Fuel expenses surged 62% from a year earlier, even as premium cabin and corporate travel revenue climbed 17% and 26%, respectively. The carrier expects to pay an average of $4.80 a gallon for fuel in the fourth quarter, up from an average price of $3.90 a gallon in the third. 
 — Deena Zaidi 
 13 Hours Ago Brad Gerstner says 'nobody knows' about future compute demand
 Brad Gerstner, Altimeter founder and CEO, speaking at the Delivering Alpha conference in New York City on Sept. 28, 2023. Adam Jeffery | CNBC Asked about embattled neocloud CoreWeave, Altimeter Capital CEO and vociferous AI bull Brad Gerstner acknowledged the uncertainty in future demand levels for computing power.
 "The reality is, nobody knows what the demand is going to be in 12 months," he told CNBC on Wednesday. "Most of us who are in the game are saying this is accelerating. We're forecasting that demand is going to accelerate. But of course there's a distribution of future unknown probabilities."
 Gerstner told CNBC earlier this month that he had taken his exposure to the AI trade down, though he didn't get into specifics during the interview .
 He reconciled his professed bullishness on AI with his diminished exposure by saying that he lives in "two simultaneous but different worlds," distinguishing between his hedge fund investments and his other investments.
 "One world is I manage money for people in a hedge fund, and so my job is to make sure I avoid some of that drawdown. In my long-only fund and in my growth funds and venture funds, we're investing in the next five to ten years," he said.
 Profitability concerns have rattled the AI trade in recent weeks as revenues coming in from frontier models Anthropic and OpenAI have disappointed analysts.
 Some on Wall Street think that AI, which is quickly becoming more of a base-level commodity than a premium product due in part to the proliferation of open-source models, is not profitable enough to substantiate trillions in capital expenditures from equipment builders.
 "We have more compute capacity than we have demand, and we have a lot of the tokens and processing power being given away in freemium solutions," John Lovelock at Gartner told CNBC on Monday. "Everyone in the AI race is running for a last-man standing position. Pretty much every market that Gartner is tracking in our AI race is likely to collapse down to a duopoly."
 — Tobias Burns 
 14 Hours Ago CME Group posts earnings and revenue beat, shares tick higher
 Sopa Images | Lightrocket | Getty Images Shares of CME Group were almost 1% higher on Wednesday after the exchange's earnings and revenue for the third quarter surpassed Wall Street's expectations.
 CME reported adjusted earnings of $3.02 per share and revenue of $1.74 billion, while analysts polled by FactSet had called for $2.99 in earnings per share and $1.71 billion in revenue.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon CME, 1-day — Sean Conlon 
 14 Hours Ago Thermo Fisher shares move higher
 Thermo Fisher Scientific shares rose more than 1% in morning trading on Wednesday, marking a turnaround from its more than 2% decline in premarket trading.
 The move comes after the company's results for the third quarter were better than expected.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon TMO, 1-day — Sean Conlon 
 15 Hours Ago Stocks open higher
 The three major averages opened Wednesday's session in the green.
 The S&P 500 rose 0.3% just after 9:30 a.m. ET, while the Nasdaq Composite gained 0.7%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average advanced 90 points, or 0.2%.
 — Sean Conlon 
 15 Hours Ago Thermo Fisher shares drop following latest quarterly results
 Thermo Fisher Scientific sign outside office building with trees and glass windows in background, South San Francisco, California, October 16, 2025. Smith Collection | Gado | Archive Photos | Getty Images Shares of Thermo Fisher Scientific dropped more than 2% in the premarket on Wednesday, even after the life sciences company reported better-than-expected results for the third quarter.
 Thermo Fisher reported adjusted earnings of $6.69 per share and $12.14 billion in revenue, above the $6.40 in earnings per share and $11.95 billion in revenue that analysts polled by FactSet had expected.
 The stock had seen sizable gains heading into the report. In the last three months, the stock has risen more than 31% through Tuesday's close. It's also up more than 18% this year.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon TMO, 3-month — Sean Conlon 
 16 Hours Ago Danaher slides after revenue miss
 Cheng Xin | Getty Images Danaher shares fell nearly 4% in premarket trading on Wednesday after the life sciences and diagnostics innovator's third-quarter revenue came up short of what analysts had expected.
 The company posted $6.55 billion in revenue, while analysts polled by FactSet had penciled in $6.56 billion.
 On the flip side, Danaher reported adjusted earnings of $2.11 per share, which was better than the $1.92 per share that analysts had anticipated. The company also raised its full-year earnings guidance.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon DHR, 1-day — Sean Conlon 
 16 Hours Ago Intuitive Surgical, SpaceX and Rocket Lab among the stocks making moves before the bell
 Check out the companies making the biggest moves premarket: 
 Intuitive Surgical — The medical robotics stock slid 6% as the company's third-quarter results failed to impress investors. Intuitive Surgical earned $3 per share, excluding certain items, on revenue of $3.05 billion.
 SpaceX — Shares gained 8% after the Elon Musk-led rocket company reported a 161% jump in third-quarter revenue to $14.58 billion. Musk also said that SpaceX and Tesla , his auto manufacturer, have formed special committees to discuss a merger. Tesla shares were up 1%.
 Space stocks — Other aerospace companies were higher following SpaceX's earnings jump. Rocket Lab rose 2.5%, while AST SpaceMobile was higher by almost 3%. Firefly Aerospace jumped 3.5%.
 Read full list here .
 — Davis Giangiulio 
 17 Hours Ago Mortgage demand falls
 Homes in San Francisco, California, US, on Thursday, Sept. 3, 2026. David Paul Morris | Bloomberg | Getty Images Mortgage demand took another leg lower, despite a brief respite from rising interest rates.
 Total mortgage application volume fell 5.3% last week compared with the previous week, according to the Mortgage Bankers Association's seasonally adjusted index.
 The average contract interest rate for 30-year fixed-rate mortgages with conforming loan balances, $832,750 or less, decreased last week to 7.41% from 7.50%, with points decreasing to 0.75 from 0.83 (including the origination fee, for loans with a 20% down payment.
 "Mortgage rates decreased for the first time in over two months," said Joel Kan, an MBA economist in a release. "However, lower rates were not enough to boost application activity, as both purchase and refinance applications continued to decline."
 Read the full story here .
 — Diana Olick 
 17 Hours Ago AT&T earnings beat expectations, but stock falls
 Sign at the entrance to an AT&T store in Manhattan. Erik Mcgregor | Lightrocket | Getty Images AT&T shares were down 4% even after the telecom giant reported better-than-expected results for the third quarter. The company earned an adjusted 65 cents per share on revenue of $32.3 billion. Analysts polled by LSEG expected a profit of 60 cents per share on revenue of $31.69 billion.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon T year to date — Fred Imbert 
 18 Hours Ago Treasury yields hold steady 
 A trader works on the floor at the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) in New York City, U.S., Sept. 28, 2026. Brendan McDermid | Reuters Treasury yields steadied early on Wednesday as investors await fresh data for insights into the U.S. economic picture ahead of next week's Federal Reserve interest rate decision.
 Yields on 10-year U.S. Treasurys — the main benchmark for mortgages, auto loans and credit card debt — were unchanged at 5.1190%.
 The yield on the 2-year Treasury note, which more closely follows short-term Federal Reserve rate decisions, was holding firm at 4.7889%.  The yield on longer-dated 30-year U.S. Treasurys — which often moves on geopolitical developments — also held steady at 5.4264%.
 — Hugh Leask 
 20 Hours Ago Asia-Pacific markets close higher as tech stocks rise
 Asia-Pacific markets closed mostly in the green on Wednesday.
 Japan's  Nikkei 225 added 0.85% to close at 64,621.24, while the Topix rose 0.86%, ending at 4,043.73.
 South Korea's Kospi gained 3.29% at 5,735.66 and the small-cap, tech-focused Kosdaq Index gained 1.38% to 792.76.
 Hong Kong's Hang Seng index was down 0.92% in its last hour of trade.
 Australia's S&P/ASX 200 ended the day 0.16% higher at 8,831.3.
 — Lee Ying Shan 
 21 Hours Ago European markets in mixed territory 
 The pan-European Stoxx 600 was flat shortly after 8:15 a.m. in London (3:15 a.m. E.T.), amid a choppy start for the continent's bourses and sectors.
 Oil and gas stocks led early gains, rising 1.11%, with technology names up 0.58%. In contrast, automakers and parts suppliers slumped 1.6%.
 Major bourses were mixed. The French CAC 40 added 0.16%, while Italy's FTSE MIB was flat. Germany's DAX dropped 0.11%, and the U.K.'s FTSE 100 fell 0.16%.
 — Hugh Leask 
 21 Hours Ago Carrefour shares plunge 10% amid French unrest
 Carrefour hypermarket in Lempdes, France, on September 18, 2026. Jerome Chabanne | Afp | Getty Images Carrefour shares plunged 10.6% in early dealmaking, after the French grocer lowered its profit forecasts and cut capex plans, citing ongoing national unrest in the country and an energy price shock to consumer sentiment.
 The supermarket giant, France's largest, also slashed its adjusted earnings per share from "high single-digit growth" to "stable to slight growth" for the year, as CEO Alexandre Bompard warned of an "unprecedented situation" in France. 
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon Carrefour. — Hugh Leask 
 21 Hours Ago UK government approves Jackdaw North Sea gas field
 The U.K. government has approved new drilling in the Jackdaw gas field in the North Sea. 
 The Jackdaw project, whose operator Adura is a joint venture between Shell and Equinor , lies about 150 miles east of Aberdeen, Scotland. 
 Adura said the field can potentially provide 6% of Britain's total gas supply, and could be connected to the U.K. grid within months. That would help boost the U.K.'s energy security at a time when the country — a net energy importer —remains vulnerable to external price shocks.
 — Hugh Leask 
 22 Hours Ago UK annual inflation rises to highest level in a year
 U.K. inflation rose by a hotter-than-expected 3.5% in the 12 months to September — its highest level in a year — driven by the surging cost of motor fuels, the Office for National Statistics said Wednesday. 
 Economists polled by Reuters had been forecasting an annual inflation rate of 3.4%.
 September's print marked a continuation of the U.K.'s upward trend for inflation, which came in at 3.1% in August and 2.9% in July. 
 — Chloe Taylor 
 22 Hours Ago Adidas shares rise in premarket after third-quarter operating profits soar 37%
 An Adidas flagship store at Nanjing Road Pedestrian Street in Shanghai, China. Cfoto | Future Publishing | Getty Images Shares in Adidas rose 3.3% in premarket trading after the German sportswear giant's preliminary third-quarter operating profit soared 37% to 1.01 billion euros ($1.13 billion). 
 Revenues increased 9% to 7.25 billion euros, as the firm revised its full-year operating profit up to 2.5 billion euros, from 2.3 billion.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon Adidas. The company said Thursday that its gross margin reached 54.3% in the three-month period, boosted by about 200 million euros in U.S. tariff refunds. 
 — Hugh Leask 
 23 Hours Ago Europe's stock markets expected to open higher
 Lights on in skyscrapers and commercial buildings on the skyline of the City of London, UK, on Tuesday, Nov. 18, 2025. U.K. business chiefs urged Chancellor of the Exchequer Rachel Reeves to ease energy costs and avoid raising the tax burden on corporate Britain as she prepares this year's budget. Bloomberg | Bloomberg | Getty Images Stoxx 50 futures were 0.42% higher as European stock markets were expected to start Wednesday's session in positive territory.
 Germany's DAX is seen opening 0.45% higher, with Italy's FTSE MIB adding 0.32% and the French CAC 40 rising 0.22%. 
 In the U.K., FTSE 100 futures were up almost 0.21%. 
 — Hugh Leask 
 24 Hours Ago Australian data center operator NextDC’s shares plunge 40% after it slashes earnings forecast
 Shares of Australia's NextDC plunged 39.5% on Wednesday after the data center operator slashed its annual earnings forecast, citing power supply delays at its Melbourne facility amid local community and stakeholder opposition.
 The company lowered its fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to between $475 million Australian dollars and A$500 million, from A$615 million to A$640 million forecast earlier, while cutting its underlying earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, or EBITDA, forecast to A$245 million to A$265 million from A$385 million to A$410 million. 
 — Jenny Lee 
 Tue, Oct 20 2026 10:09 PM EDT CATL shares fall over 9% following third-quarter results
 Shares of Chinese battery giant CATL fell 9.1% in Hong Kong and 9.2% in China on Wednesday after the company released its third-quarter results on Tuesday.
 The company reported a 14.5% year-on-year rise in third-quarter net profit attributable to shareholders to 21.25 billion yuan ($3.18 billion), while revenue jumped 58.6% to 165.22 billion yuan.
 Citi maintained its Buy rating on CATL but cut its 2026–2028 earnings forecasts by 9%, 14% and 15%, respectively, and lowered its price target for the company's Shenzhen-listed shares to 479 yuan from 500 yuan.
 The bank said CATL's third-quarter net profit missed its expectations, citing weaker gross margins, higher expenses and impairment losses.
 — Jenny Lee 
 Tue, Oct 20 2026 10:08 PM EDT South Korea's stock exchange temporarily halts program trading 
 South Korea's stock exchange briefly halted program trading after Kospi 200 futures surged 5%, triggering a so-called "sidecar" mechanism designed to curb excessive market volatility.
 The five-minute trading curb came as South Korean equities staged a sharp rebound on Wednesday, with technology and semiconductor stocks recovering from a bruising sell-off earlier this week as investors assess prospects of the artificial-intelligence sector.
 The benchmark Kospi Index was up 4.4%.
 — Lee Ying Shan 
 Tue, Oct 20 2026 8:59 PM EDT Japan exports post huge miss in September as growth slows to 16.7%
 Japan's exports in September rose 16.7% from a year earlier, missing market expectations by a huge margin. Reuters-polled analysts had pegged exports growth at 20.1%.
 This is the second straight month that shipments from Japan have recorded a slowdown, after hitting a near four-year high in July.
 Growth was supported by continued strong semiconductor exports, with shipments rising 49.4% year on year by value.
 Exports of machinery also bolstered growth, with semiconductor-related machinery shipments up 43.9% and power generation machinery exports climbing 22.6%.
 In terms of destinations, shipments to mainland China — Japan's largest trading partner — rose 8.6%, while exports to the U.S. climbed 22.9%.
 — Lim Hui Jie 
 Tue, Oct 20 2026 8:45 PM EDT Asia tech stocks rebound as AI optimism returns; Elice surges nearly 30% after bruising debut
 Asian technology stocks staged a broad rebound on Wednesday as optimism surrounding SpaceX's latest quarterly results helped revive sentiment toward artificial intelligence infrastructure investments following a bruising selloff. 
 South Korean memory chip giant SK Hynix surging 6.38%, while rival Samsung Electronics climbed 5.03%.
 Shares of South Korean artificial intelligence infrastructure provider Elice soared 29.92%, recovering ground after plunging over 30% in its trading debut Tuesday. The sharp reversal came after the company's disappointing debut reignited concerns over whether heavy spending on AI infrastructure would translate into sustainable profits.
 Japanese semiconductor stocks also rallied, with chip-testing equipment maker Advantest jumping 5.31%, while Tokyo Electron gained 3.02%. Technology investment giant SoftBank Group rose 4.70%.
 "The SpaceX quarter and what this indicates for the neoclouds is very bullish globally and the Korean stocks have sold off way too much in my view," said Dan Ives, Tech Analyst at Yorkville Ives.
 — Lee Ying Shan 
 Tue, Oct 20 2026 8:08 PM EDT Japan's Nikkei 225 rises over 1%, South Korean stocks gain 2%
 Asia-Pacific markets opened higher on Wednesday, with South Korean stocks leading gains.
 The Kospi advanced 1.8%, rebounding from Tuesday's losses, while the tech-focused Kosdaq Index jumped over 2%.
 Japan's  Nikkei 225 was up 1.4%, while the Topix added 0.93%.
 Australia's S&P/ASX 200 was flat.
 — Lee Ying Shan 
 Tue, Oct 20 2026 7:31 PM EDT Asia-Pacific markets set to rebound after Wall Street gains on strong earnings, easing oil prices
 Asia-Pacific markets were set to open higher Wednesday, after Wall Street rose overnight on the back of strong corporate earnings and easing oil prices.
 Futures for Japan's  Nikkei 225  in Chicago were at 65,355, while in Osaka they were lats at 65,210, compared with the index's previous close of 64,075.42
 Futures for Hong Kong's Hang Seng index last traded at 24,001, higher than the index's last close of 23,867.74.
 Australia's S&P/ASX 200 gained 0.27%.
 — Lee Ying Shan 
 Tue, Oct 20 2026 6:31 PM EDT Stocks making the biggest moves after hours: SpaceX, Netflix & more
 Check out some of the companies making the biggest moves after hours: 
 Intuitive Surgical — The medical robotics stock fell about 7% as the company's third-quarter results failed to impress investors. Intuitive Surgical earned $3 per share, excluding certain items, on revenue of $3.05 billion.
 SpaceX — Shares gained almost 7% after the Elon Musk-led rocket company reported a 161% jump in third-quarter revenue to $14.58 billion. Musk also said that SpaceX and Tesla , his auto manufacturer, have formed special committees to discuss a merger. Tesla shares were up 1%.
 Netflix — Shares of Netflix fell more than 5% after the streaming giant reported third quarter revenue that was in line with Wall Street's expectations. Sales came in at $12.87 billion, up 12% year over year, boosted by growth in membership and an increase in subscription prices that went into effect in March, the company said.
 Read more about Tuesday's after-hours movers here .
 — Darla Mercado 
 Tue, Oct 20 2026 6:24 PM EDT U.S. stock futures open higher Tuesday night
 U.S. stock futures were up Tuesday night as traders weighed the latest round of earnings reports.
 Futures tied to the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.19%. S&P 500 futures gained 0.47% and Nasdaq-100 futures added nearly 1%.
 — Deena Zaidi
